title: What would happen if you fell into a black hole?
sources: Stephen Hawking A Brief History of Time

lines.text: What would actually happen to your body if you fell into a cosmic supermassive black hole?
lines.caps: What happens if | you fall into | a *black hole?

lines.text: As you drift toward the event horizon, extreme gravitational tidal forces begin stretching space.
The pull on your feet would be vastly stronger than the pull on your head.
lines.caps: Gravity on your *feet | is vastly stronger than your *head!

lines.text: Your body would be vertically stretched and horizontally compressed like a string of dough.
lines.caps: Your body gets *stretched | into a noodle of *atoms

lines.text: Astrophysicists call this gruesome cosmic phenomenon spaghettification.
To an outside observer, you would appear to slow down and freeze at the event horizon forever.
lines.caps: To outsiders you *freeze | at the event horizon *forever

lines.text: Crossing the threshold of a black hole is a one-way trip beyond the edge of physics itself.
lines.caps: A one-way journey *beyond | the laws of *physics!
